uncited: It differs from [Brute-Force QEF Solver](4403-brute-force-qef-solver.md) by optimizing the conditioning of the matrix system rather than just accumulating errors, and from [QEF Solver Initialization](4722-qef-solver-initialization.md) by actively modifying the right-hand side vector to reflect the shifted coordinate system.
**Compute Centroid:** Calculate the mass point (centroid) $M$ as the average of the input points.
**Adjust Right-Hand Side:** Compute the adjustment term $T = A M$.
**Time Complexity:** Dominated by the SVD solve, typically $O(1)$ for fixed-size $3 \times 3$ systems, but depends on the number of SVD sweeps.
**Limitations:** Requires pre-computation of the centroid and matrix-vector multiplication overhead.
**When to use:** When intersection points are far from the cell origin or when standard QEF solvers fail to converge due to precision loss.
It is a practical implementation detail for robust dual contouring rather than a widely published academic algorithm with a distinct citation.
